summary.headline: Windows Security Center MTD connector now requires manual MAM enablement
summary.summary: The Edge data-security setup now instructs admins to open the Windows Security Center connector after creating it, enable Connect Windows devices for MAM, and save. It also changes the documented state from Unavailable after creation to Available, becoming Enabled after the toggle is turned on.
summary.adminImpact: After creating this connector, explicitly enable Connect Windows devices for MAM and verify the connector reports Enabled before relying on it for MAM.

summary.headline: Updated Autopilot device-preparation app documentation links
summary.summary: The automatic-mode tutorial replaces outdated links for Win32 packaging, Enterprise App Catalog apps, and the Win32 management overview with their current documentation destinations.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change is described; use the updated links when preparing supported app assignments.

summary.headline: Updated Win32 package link in automatic device-preparation policy tutorial
summary.summary: The Windows 365 Frontline shared-mode automatic policy tutorial now links to the current Win32 package creation article instead of the prior Win32 packaging path.
summary.adminImpact: No policy behavior changed; follow the current package-creation guidance when adding Win32 apps.

summary.headline: Updated user-driven device-preparation app guidance links
summary.summary: The Entra join user-driven tutorial refreshes links for Win32 package creation, Enterprise App Catalog app creation, and Win32 app management.
summary.adminImpact: No change to supported app types is stated; use the replacement links for current assignment instructions.

summary.headline: Updated supported-app links in user-driven Autopilot policy tutorial
summary.summary: The user-driven Entra join policy tutorial changes its Win32 and Enterprise App Catalog references to the current package and catalog-app articles.
summary.adminImpact: No configuration change is described; use the updated references when selecting apps for device preparation.

summary.headline: Updated Enterprise App Catalog reference in device-preparation release notes
summary.summary: The device-preparation What's New entry continues to describe Enterprise App Catalog support and now points to the renamed catalog-app creation article.
summary.adminImpact: No release behavior changed; update internal bookmarks to the current Enterprise App Catalog guidance.

summary.headline: Updated Enterprise App Catalog reference in Autopilot release notes
summary.summary: The Autopilot What's New entry for Enterprise App Catalog blocking apps now links to the current catalog-app creation article.
summary.adminImpact: No enrollment-status-page behavior changed; use the updated link when configuring catalog apps.

summary.headline: Intune Management Extension minimum-version notice removed from In development
summary.summary: The in-development article no longer lists the requirement for Windows devices to run Intune Management Extension 1.58.103.0 or later; the notice was moved to What's New.
summary.adminImpact: Check the What's New guidance and ensure Windows devices can sync so they receive the Intune Management Extension update.

summary.headline: Intune Management Extension 1.58.103.0 is now the required minimum
summary.summary: What's New states that Windows devices must run Intune Management Extension 1.58.103.0 or later. Earlier versions no longer receive IME-dependent configurations or updates, including Win32 deployments, PowerShell scripts, remediations, and platform scripts.
summary.adminImpact: Verify managed Windows devices can sync with Intune and are on IME 1.58.103.0 or later before depending on those workloads.

summary.headline: Userless visionOS and tvOS ADE notice removed from In development
summary.summary: The in-development article removes the planned userless Automated Device Enrollment capability for visionOS and tvOS because the feature was moved to What's New.
summary.adminImpact: Use the released guidance when planning Apple Vision Pro or Apple TV enrollment rather than treating the capability as in development.

summary.headline: Userless ADE is supported for visionOS and tvOS
summary.summary: Intune now supports userless Apple Automated Device Enrollment for Apple Vision Pro and Apple TV through Apple Business Manager or School Manager, including custom settings uploads, default enrollment restrictions, and device actions. It requires Intune Plan 2 and tvOS or visionOS 26 or later.
summary.adminImpact: Confirm Plan 2 licensing and supported OS versions, then configure ADE without user affinity for eligible Apple TV and Vision Pro devices.

summary.headline: Apple service-access management notice removed from In development
summary.summary: The planned Apple access-management entry was removed from In development after being moved to What's New.
summary.adminImpact: Refer to the released Apple service-access guidance when setting organization-owned Apple device controls.

summary.headline: Apple service-access management is now available
summary.summary: Intune documentation now describes Apple access-management settings in Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager for controlling which organization-owned devices users can sign in to and which apps and services are available to Apple accounts.
summary.adminImpact: Review Apple Business Manager or School Manager service-access settings for organization-owned iOS, iPadOS, and macOS devices.
